privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: InSeconds (IN//SECONDS) is a free music blind test game, available at https://inseconds.cc. It remains fully playable as a guest, without any account or registration; creating an account, using only an email address, is optional and lets you find your progress again on another device. This policy describes, in accordance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR — Regulation EU 2016/679), the personal data processing carried out by the application.

controller.title: Data controller
controller.body:
The data controller is the publisher of the InSeconds website, an individual based in France, who can be reached at the contact address given at the bottom of this page. InSeconds is a personal project, developed in the publisher's free time, with no associated commercial entity.
No Data Protection Officer (DPO) has been appointed: given the volume and nature of the data processed (no sensitive data, no profiling), this is not required under the GDPR. The publisher remains your single point of contact for any question about your data.

data.title: Data collected, purposes and legal basis

cookie.title: Cookie
cookie.body:
A single technical cookie ("authToken") is set, whether you play as a guest or with an account. It contains your identifier in encrypted form and is used exclusively to run the game (recognizing your browser, resuming a game). It lasts 90 days from your last visit.
If you create an account, logging in from another device (via the link received by email) sets a new cookie specific to that device, linked to the same account — each device keeps its own cookie.
This cookie is strictly necessary to provide the service: in line with the ePrivacy rules and the guidelines of the French data protection authority (CNIL), it is exempt from prior consent and therefore does not require a consent banner.
No advertising cookies, trackers or audience measurement tools are used.

retention.title: Data retention
retention.body:
Game data (answers, scores, win streak) is kept for the lifetime of your identifier or account, to feed your history and the anonymous global statistics shown to players.
For a guest player, this data is never linked to a real identity: only a random technical identifier connects you to your games.
If you create an account, your history is linked to your email address — that is precisely what lets you find it again on another device. This data is permanently deleted when your account is deleted, or upon simple request (see "Your rights").
The login link sent by email is valid for only 15 minutes and can be used only once; after that time, or once used, it becomes permanently invalid.

thirdParties.title: Recipients, hosting and transfers outside the EU

deezer.title: Legal notice — music content (Deezer API)
deezer.body:
Music excerpts (30 seconds), album covers and metadata (artist, title) are provided by the Deezer API and used in keeping with its terms of use (Deezer API Terms of Use), on a strictly non-commercial basis: InSeconds is free, ad-free and generates no revenue.
This content remains the exclusive property of Deezer and its respective rights holders (artists, producers, labels). It is streamed for illustrative purposes within the game, with no download capability, and each track links to its official Deezer page for full listening.
Deezer is a registered trademark of Deezer S.A. InSeconds is an independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Deezer.

security.title: Data security

rights.title: Your rights
rights.body:
In accordance with Articles 15 to 21 of the GDPR, you have the right to access, rectify, erase, restrict the processing of, object to the processing of, and port the data associated with your identifier or account (email, pseudo, game history, current streak). If you created an account, you may also withdraw your consent at any time, without affecting the lawfulness of processing carried out before that withdrawal.
Deletion permanently erases your game history, your current streak and, where applicable, your email and pseudo.
You also have the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority (in France, the CNIL — www.cnil.fr).
